original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-h1-invertible}
Let $(\mathcal{C}, \mathcal{O})$ be a locally ringed site.
There is a canonical isomorphism
$$
H^1(\mathcal{C}, \mathcal{O}^*) = \Pic(\mathcal{O}).
$$
of abelian groups.

stage_a_original_draft:
For a locally ringed site $(\mathcal C,\mathcal O)$, let $\mathcal O^*$ be the sheaf of multiplicative units of $\mathcal O$, and let $\operatorname{Pic}(\mathcal O)$ be the abelian group of isomorphism classes of invertible $\mathcal O$-modules, with multiplication given by tensor product. The group $H^1(\mathcal C,\mathcal O^*)$ denotes first sheaf cohomology of the abelian sheaf $\mathcal O^*$.

Let $(\mathcal{C}, \mathcal{O})$ be a locally ringed site.
There is a canonical isomorphism
$$
H^1(\mathcal{C}, \mathcal{O}^*) = \Pic(\mathcal{O}).
$$
of abelian groups.

The group $H^1(\mathcal C,\mathcal O^*)$ denotes first sheaf cohomology of the abelian sheaf $\mathcal O^*$.

Let $(\mathcal{C}, \mathcal{O})$ be a locally ringed site.
There is a canonical isomorphism
$$
H^1(\mathcal{C}, \mathcal{O}^*) = \Pic(\mathcal{O}).
$$
of abelian groups.
hypotheses: $(\mathcal C,\mathcal O)$ is a locally ringed site.
conclusions: There is a canonical isomorphism of abelian groups $H^1(\mathcal C,\mathcal O^*)\cong\operatorname{Pic}(\mathcal O)$.
